html:
The Island of Mozambique is a small coral island off northern Mozambique, a Swahili trading town when Vasco da Gama landed there in 1498, and the capital of Portuguese East Africa until 1898.

It was ruled by a sheikh linked to the Swahili coast, whose name may have given the whole country its name. The Portuguese built the great fortress of São Sebastião in the 16th century, which held off Dutch attacks in 1607 and 1608, and used the island as a base on the route to India.

The island traded ivory, gold and later slaves, and its stone town of churches, mosques and palaces was listed by UNESCO in 1991. The capital moved to Lourenço Marques in 1898, and the island became quiet. It recalls the first contact of da Gama with the Swahili world.
sum: The Island of Mozambique is a small coral island off northern Mozambique, a Swahili trading town when Vasco da Gama landed there in 1498, and the capital of Portuguese East Africa until 1898.
